items.title: Output isn't design
items.summary: Linear's founder makes the case that the real work of design is figuring out what should exist and why, not the act of producing a polished screen. AI can spit out interfaces fast, but mistaking that output for design gives you products that look slick and fall apart in use.
items.why: You're deciding how AI fits into how designers work at Cuemath — this is a clear, founder-level argument for keeping judgment and problem-framing at the centre rather than letting tools auto-generate the answer.

items.title: Durable Patterns in AI Product Design
items.summary: A veteran product designer lays out the handful of interface ideas that keep working as AI products evolve from simple chat to multi-step agents: suggesting next questions, showing sources so people trust answers, and letting users hide or reveal the messy detail of what the AI is doing.
items.why: A practical checklist of what actually works in AI interfaces, useful as you shape AI-assisted features in the Cuemath app rather than guessing at patterns from scratch.

items.title: Autonomy, Relatedness, and Competence in UX Design
items.summary: Walks through the three things psychology says people need to stay motivated — a sense of choice, feeling connected to others, and feeling capable — and shows how products like Duolingo and Minecraft build them in (and how clumsy apps break them).
items.why: This is the motivation research that sits directly under your belts, XP, and levels work — a clean re-grounding before the next call on how the app keeps kids coming back.

items.title: Tools for Thought as Cultural Practices, not Computational Objects
items.summary: Argues that the phrase 'tools for thought' has been hijacked by note-taking apps, when really it covers much older human inventions — writing, maps, mathematical notation, the back-and-forth of Socratic questioning — that all expanded what our minds can do.
items.why: A useful lens for designing how kids genuinely build mathematical understanding, since maths notation itself is one of these thinking tools rather than just content to drill.

items.title: Htag magazine
items.summary: A Belgian HR magazine that deliberately ignores how dull business publications usually look. It runs three typefaces with clear jobs — a bold one for headlines, a readable serif for long text, a plain one for labels — plus strong colour blocks and an off-kilter grid.
items.why: A tidy worked example of giving each typeface a defined role, the same discipline you apply to the CueDesign type system and Cuemath's editorial work.

items.title: New Logo and Identity for Lithuanian Culture Institute by andstudio
items.summary: A quick before-and-after look at the rebrand of Lithuania's national culture body, where andstudio replaced the old mark with a colourful, square-based geometric system under the title 'Fair and Square'. The detailed write-up sits behind Brand New's paywall; the logo comparison is the free part.
items.why: A national-institution identity built from a simple geometric building block, the kind of system thinking that maps onto how a brand like Cuemath scales one idea across many touchpoints.
